newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Greece plans to spend six trillion drachmas on armaments, an amount that will burden the convergence programme to bring Greece's economy in line with the rest of the European Union.

--Three names hold the key to uncovering the details of the scandal at the stock exchange. Trading resumed yesterday after a three-day closure, with 50 of listed members trading and the rest expected to have settled their transactions today.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis declares himself uncocnerned by possible adverse reactions coming from ruling party PASOK regarding the government's economic choices. Simitis says there are dissenting opinions within the party on how to apply a just economic policy but that all agreed that the aim was to achieve convergence.

--Traditional celebrations marking the anniversary of the 1973 students' uprising against the military junta then ruling Greece kick off with a bomb. "Fighting Resistance Front" claims responsibility for the explosion at the Athens Polytechnic School last night.

--Simitis yesterday asks for sacrifices to ensure Greece can get the 16 trillion drachmas needed to pay for its armaments programme. The greater part of the programme's cost will be covered by foreign lending.
--The mayor of Athens urges residents to not take out the rubbish for four days, as municipalities and the Athens rubbish dump shuts down.
--The captain of the 'Kriti Sea' is fined 150 million drachmas for pollution and Motor Oil looks set to pay out 100 million for the same case.
--The US initiative on normalisation of Greek-Turkish relations takes on form as Washington works on its initiative to resolve the Cyprus problem.
--Relatives of the four seamen missing since the sinking of the Kostakos gunboat plead with National Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos to continue searches for their bodies.

--New reports state that the four missing seamen were trapped alive in the sinking gunboat and unable to escape because the emergency exit was padlocked. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
